prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1214; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a side impact at an intersection involving the insured's vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant reports neck strain and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. No concerns with coverage identification at this stage.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at impact and records the collision as described by the claimant.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who gave an account matching the claimant's description of how the crash occurred. Photos from the scene are consistent with a side impact at the intersection.

Entry 5: Took a recorded statement from the claimant. The account of the collision was the same as the one given at first notice of loss.

Entry 6: Reviewed the injury report. The neck strain fits the direction and force of the impact. No prior treatment to the neck or upper back appears in available records.

Entry 7: Inspected the vehicle and noted damage to the driver's side. Prior inspection records show no earlier damage to this vehicle. Some of the visible damage may have come from a different source, so the extent attributable to this impact has not been settled.

Entry 8: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for a strain of this type. Requested updated treatment notes to review the course of care.

Entry 9: Spoke with the claimant again. The account has stayed consistent across every contact. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage period. Will continue reviewing the treatment records and the vehicle damage estimate before deciding next steps.
